acceptance.requirement: The same canonical DAG, selector receipt, validated layered investigation projection, and runtime facts produce the same eligibility and frontier digests regardless of input order or computedAt.
readyFrontier is the exact maximum eligible member-issue plus stage set; root-authored status cannot omit or add members.
Every blocked active member has compiler-owned, canonically ordered, directly evidence-bound reason enums.
Completed tombstones unlock dependents and reopen or tombstone drift removes them from the frontier.
An empty frontier is valid only when every active member has a blocker, active attempt, or unchanged terminal reason.
Ready work plus available slots and no root-only delivery action produces a non-empty maximal dispatch set.

A validated candidate-ready layered projection may enter only test-contract-ready; shallower phases expose investigation-incomplete with blocked time and owner identity, while later stages require dispatch-investigated.
Selector/comment, base, scope, layered freshness/digest, terminal, and role-permission drift invalidate old eligibility input digests.
Local stage progress recomputes the execution frontier without triggering a semantic DAG update.
Array, issue, and traversal reordering do not change canonical digests.
Fifteen eligible independent members fill fifteen available slots, while N eligible members produce exactly N candidates.
Each issue has exactly one deterministic next stage and cannot dispatch test and implementation writers together.
UI behavior green advances to independent UX acceptance before documentation or delivery.
Documentation completion advances to delivery, and delivery completion advances to cleanup before closure.
Root consumes compiler projections and cannot edit eligibility, reasons, or the current stage.
Sol/max test-owner and Sol/low implementation candidates, write permissions, and authority digests are eligibility inputs.
A UI issue rejects an ordinary code implementer or missing design Skill/authority digest.
Group overlays retain independent per-member eligibility and cannot make a blocked member ready.
Group green cannot hide an individual member behavior failure.
Ineligible grouping falls back to per-issue dispatch and cannot serialize independent low-conflict members.
The #1816 fixture and production compiler consume one validated discovery/classification/dispatch investigation projection and never node.investigation.
Projection and layer digests are recomputed and bound to the selected member facts; arbitrary 64-hex values are not authority.

Discovery and classification authoredBy facts exactly bind role=dag-creator-updater, model=gpt-5.6-sol, effort=max, executionClass=observe-only, freshContext=true authority; dispatch investigation exactly binds the frozen Sol/max write-tests-only test owner and testOwnerId.

Discovery and classification bind the exact non-root DAG actor identity and the same actorId across both semantic layers; dispatch binds the frozen contract testOwnerId rather than trusting a self-consistent replacement identity.
Every discovery layer independently binds its exact schema, complete status, and recomputed inputDigest; re-signing the outer layer digest cannot authorize changed envelope or source inputs.

The validated projection binds its exact schema, exact machine read-only validation actor, one projection member per DAG member, and testOwnerCandidates/implementationReady recomputed from member phases.
check-dag-gate passes the validated layered investigation projection into frontier validation; importing or storing it without consumption is insufficient.
Production dot or bracket reads of node.investigation and any compatibility fallback are forbidden; legacy input is rejected rather than replayed as dispatch authority.
